How to read these rules

Daily loss is not one rule. HyroTrader and Mubite measure from your equity at 00:00 UTC, Crypto Fund Trader from the balance at 00:05 UTC, Bitfunded from the starting balance on a UTC+8 day, FTMO at midnight Central European time, IQ Capital has none on its Core challenge (it caps each position at 1% instead), and Breakout (by its own page as quoted) from the 00:30 UTC balance with open positions excluded. An open position losing money at the reset can therefore count against you at one firm and not at another.

Static beats trailing of the same size. Every crypto plan above uses a static maximum drawdown except FTMO's 1-Step and IQ Capital's Core, which trail the highest end-of-day balance or equity. A trailing floor follows your profit up, so it is tighter than its number suggests once you are ahead.

Leverage is not comparable as one figure. HyroTrader allows up to 150x in the test and then caps total exposure at twice the balance once funded; Breakout and Bitfunded stop at 5x; the CFD firms sit near 1:1 to 1:3.3. Train at the leverage you will be allowed once funded, not the one the test allows.

FAQ

Which crypto prop firm has the easiest rules?
None is easy in the way that matters: the daily loss limit (3-5% on every plan here except IQ Capital's Core, which has none and caps each position at 1% instead) fails far more challenges than the target. Looser drawdown usually costs a lower target elsewhere or a two-step evaluation. Compare the daily loss limit and how it is measured first - equity or balance, and at which hour - then the drawdown type.
What is the difference between static and trailing drawdown?
A static floor sits a fixed distance below the starting balance and never moves. A trailing floor rises with your highest balance (or highest end-of-day balance), so profit you give back counts against you. A 6% trailing drawdown is much tighter than a 6% static one once you are in profit.
Can I practise a crypto prop firm challenge for free?
Yes - MarginPad runs the same three rule shapes (one-step, two-step and end-of-day trailing) on a free paper account with live prices, and our server enforces the daily loss and drawdown the way a firm does. It funds nobody, but a pass tells you whether you can do it before you pay for an evaluation.
Do these prices include a refund?
Some firms refund the evaluation fee with the first payout (HyroTrader on its One-Step and Two-Step, Mubite on its Two-Step, Bitfunded on the third payout); others never refund it. Prices change and discount banners at checkout change them again - always read the firm's own checkout.
